stories.headline: Sakura-Con Closes Out With Cosplay, Panels & Pure Magic
stories.body: The Pacific Northwest's longest-running anime convention wraps its final day at Seattle Convention Center today, April 5. Expect an epic exhibitor hall, cosplay that rivals anything you've seen on the internet, cultural panels, and industry guests. Even if you just show up to people-watch, it's absolutely worth the trip Downtown.
stories.location: Downtown · Today, April 5 (final day), 8 AM–5 PM

stories.headline: Scorsese on Screen Every Wednesday at SIFF Cinema Uptown
stories.body: SIFF is screening Martin Scorsese's films every Wednesday night through April 29, paired with essays from poet and film curator Tova Gannana — a proper masterclass for your midweek. The series kicks off with 1973's Mean Streets and closes with The Irishman. Tickets run $18–$160 depending on the package.
stories.location: Lower Queen Anne · Every Wednesday through April 29

stories.headline: Broadway Touring Musical Hits the Paramount April 7–10
stories.body: A big touring musical production rolls into the Paramount Theatre for four nights only, April 7–10, with large-scale staging and a full orchestra. The Paramount's ornate hall makes every seat feel like a front-row experience. Snag tickets before they disappear — touring shows like this sell fast in Seattle.

stories.headline: Capitol Hill Week Celebrates the Neighborhood You Love
stories.body: From April 9–15, Capitol Hill Week shines a spotlight on the businesses, bars, and creative spaces that make the Hill the Hill. Grab a free pass, unlock special deals from local businesses, and check in around the neighborhood for a chance to win a $200 Visa gift card. Kick things off at The Stranger's office during Capitol Hill Art Walk on April 9, 6–8 PM.

stories.headline: Skagit Valley Tulip Festival Blooms All April Long
stories.body: Just 60 miles north of Seattle, the Skagit Valley Tulip Festival fills the entire month of April with jaw-dropping fields of color, farm stands, and seasonal events. It's the PNW's most photogenic road trip and the only socially acceptable reason to wake up before 7 AM on a weekday. Bring rain boots — and your camera.
stories.location: Mount Vernon, Skagit Valley · All of April

stories.headline: The Big Taste Brings Seattle's Best Bites to Magnuson Park
stories.body: On Sunday, April 12, Hangar 30 at Magnuson Park transforms into a foodie paradise for The Big Taste, a food and wine event featuring local restaurants and beverage producers. It's one of the most community-driven eat-and-drink events of the spring season. Grab your tickets early — this one draws a crowd.
stories.location: Sand Point / Magnuson Park · Sunday, April 12

stories.headline: Seattle Cherry Blossom Festival Returns to Seattle Center April 10–12
stories.body: The Seattle Cherry Blossom & Japanese Cultural Festival blooms at Seattle Center April 10–12, featuring cultural performances, food vendors, and exhibits celebrating Japanese heritage. It's one of the most beloved spring traditions in the city and completely free to attend. Pack a picnic blanket and let the blossoms do the rest.
stories.location: Seattle Center, Lower Queen Anne · April 10–12
